title: [CQ-F06] Served context identity
description:
Objective: Persist served context on existing attempts and expose revision, approved revision, attempt/generation and packet/receipt identities.

Deliverable: Served context identity. This is task F06 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F05.
definitionOfDone: Default/full context can create durable receipts; status-only polls cannot.
Receipt binds worker and receiving process/session incarnation as well as task/attempt/revision.
Failed persistence cannot yield a valid strict receipt.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Schema: add the served-context receipt shape (types only, no behaviour). In packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, directly after `interface ExecutionAttempt`, add:
`export interface ServedContextReceipt { id: string; packetId: string; taskId: string; attemptId: string; generation: number; workerId: string; sessionId: string; planRevision: number; approvedPlanRevision?: number; view: 'default' | 'full'; servedAt: string }`
and give ExecutionAttempt an optional last field `contextReceipt?: ServedContextReceipt`.

Brief doc comments in the file's style:
- It is the latest get_context packet served to THIS attempt's own worker for one receiving session.
- Written only by attemptStore.recordContextReceipt and persisted before it is served. A later receipt replaces it. Never backfilled. Purely additive: no migration, no schemaVersion bump.
- id is 'ctxreceipt-<32 hex>'. packetId is 'sha256:<64 hex>' of the served payload without its servedContext block.
- sessionId is the receiving session's incarnation exactly as its runner names it: the wrapper's MOE_SESSION_ID `<workerId>@<preflight-iso>`, minted once per CLI launch. The daemon never derives it, and it is never evidence of liveness.
- planRevision is the task's revision when served.
- approvedPlanRevision is Task.approvedPlanRevision when that was a non-negative safe integer, else ABSENT. Never null: that is the F04 rule.
- view names which non-status read was served.

State plainly: a receipt records what was served to whom. It is never approval, model understanding, readiness or liveness, and a packet id never substitutes for plan approval (approval stays Task.approvedPlanRevision === Task.planRevision).

Delivery: this file is a CONTESTED path. Follow the Delivery note in planningNotes.risks.

Store: persist the receipt on the existing attempt record. In packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts, follow recordAttemptPresence's validate → writeEntity → map.set idiom. NEVER route through setAttemptPhase: lastPhaseAt is the reconcile-window clock.

(a) `export function readContextSessionId(value: unknown): string | undefined`
- undefined → undefined.
- Anything else must pass `validateStringValue(value, 'sessionId', { maxLength: 255 })` from ./validators.js. That helper imports only leaf modules, so there is no cycle. 255 is record_commit's sessionId bound.
- Non-string, blank, NUL/CR/LF or >255 chars → INVALID_INPUT. No trim, no truncation, no coercion. null is refused, not treated as absent.

(b) `export function readContextReceipt(value: unknown): ServedContextReceipt | undefined`. This is the ONE definition of a valid receipt, used on every write and by later readers (F07).
- undefined → undefined.
- Otherwise it must be a plain object whose enumerable own key SET is exactly the required keys plus the optional approvedPlanRevision. Compare key sets, not count+hasOwn (mem gotcha-strict-decoder-key-set).
- id, taskId, attemptId, workerId and servedAt are non-blank strings.
- packetId matches /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/.
- sessionId is required and validated via (a).
- generation is a positive safe integer.
- planRevision, and approvedPlanRevision when present, are non-negative safe integers.
- view is 'default' or 'full'.
- Anything malformed → INVALID_INPUT (field 'contextReceipt' or 'contextReceipt.<field>'), never coerced.
- Returns a fresh primitive-only object in canonical key order: id, packetId, taskId, attemptId, generation, workerId, sessionId, planRevision, approvedPlanRevision?, view, servedAt.

(c) `export async function recordContextReceipt(state, p: { attemptId: string; workerId: string; sessionId: string; packetId: string; planRevision: number; approvedPlanRevision?: number; view: 'default' | 'full' }): Promise<ServedContextReceipt>`.
Error handling, in this order and all before any write:
1. requireNonBlank attemptId.
2. A missing record → NOT_FOUND, codeName ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND (the setAttemptPhase shape).
3. phase !== 'running' → STATE_CONFLICT, codeName ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING, context { attemptId, taskId, phase }. Use the local conflict() helper; no enum edit.
4. p.workerId !== record.workerId → NOT_ALLOWED.
Then build the receipt:
- Binding fields come from the STORED attempt, never from the caller: taskId, attemptId = record.id, generation via decodeStoredGeneration, workerId.
- Add id = generateId('ctxreceipt') and servedAt = new Date().toISOString().
- Pass the whole receipt through (b).
Persist `{ ...record, contextReceipt }` with state.writeEntity('attempts', id, …), THEN state.attempts.set. A rejected write throws and leaves the map and disk exactly as they were. Return a copy.
Latest wins: the new receipt replaces any earlier one, and phase, lastPhaseAt, presence and every other field are carried over unchanged. The caller holds state.mutex.

(d) detached(): also structuredClone a present contextReceipt. When neither a snapshot nor a receipt exists, keep returning the stored object itself, so every existing record's behaviour is unchanged.

Add one header-comment line naming this write. No activity row and no emit, per the store convention.

Tests: CREATE packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContextReceipt.test.ts with the store cases:
- recordContextReceipt refusals before any write (writeEntity spy not called, stored record toStrictEqual unchanged):
  - unknown attempt → ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND
  - closed and finalizing attempts → ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING
  - another worker → NOT_ALLOWED
  - packetId 'sha256:abc', planRevision -1 and 1.5, approvedPlanRevision -1, view 'status' → INVALID_INPUT
  Assert codeName/code, not only the message.
- readContextReceipt:
  - undefined → undefined
  - a valid receipt round-trips to an equal but distinct object
  - an extra key, a missing key and a wrong-typed field → INVALID_INPUT
- Mutating getAttempt(...).contextReceipt does not alter the stored record.
- recordAttemptPresence keeps the receipt.
Use it.each tables and shared seed helpers.

get_context: expose the identities and record receipts. In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContext.ts:

(a) inputSchema gains `sessionId: { type: 'string', description }`. The description says:
- It is the receiving session's incarnation exactly as its runner names it, e.g. the agent wrapper's MOE_SESSION_ID `<workerId>@<preflight-iso>`. The daemon never derives it.
- With it, a default or view:"full" read by the worker that owns the task's running attempt records a durable served-context receipt on that attempt. view:"status" never does.
- It is non-blank, at most 255 chars, with no NUL or line breaks; anything else is refused.
NO env fallback: never read process.env.MOE_SESSION_ID. The daemon must not mint a receiver identity, and seat env leaks into tests.

(b) Right after the existing view check, before task resolution and before any write: `const sessionId = readContextSessionId(params.sessionId)`. A malformed value refuses EVERY view, status included, with INVALID_INPUT and writes nothing (contextFetchedBy is not stamped).

(c) Keep the view:"status" early return exactly as it is. It never builds or records a receipt (DoD1).

(d) Add `servedContextIdentity(state, task, packet, { view: 'default' | 'full', workerId: callerWorkerId, sessionId })`, modelled on executionPolicyContext.
Error handling: it never throws.
Identity:
- taskId.
- planRevision = decodeStoredPlanRevision(task) from ../state/taskStore.js, in try/catch; null when unreadable.
- attempt = currentAttempt(state, task.id), in try/catch, because a hand-edited deep record overflows structuredClone (mem gotcha-daemon-detached-clone-overflows-on-deep-json); null when unreadable.
- approvedPlanRevision = task.approvedPlanRevision when it is a non-negative safe integer, else null.
- attemptId and generation from the open attempt, else null.
receiptStatus precedence:
1. 'identity-unreadable': either read failed.
2. 'no-session': sessionId is undefined.
3. 'no-running-attempt': no open attempt, or its phase !== 'running'.
4. 'not-attempt-owner': callerWorkerId is empty, attempt.workerId !== caller, or task.assignedWorkerId !== caller.
5. Otherwise record.
Every non-recorded status returns receiptId: null and packetId: null, and hashes and writes NOTHING. That keeps unrecorded payloads deterministic: getContext.test.ts compares whole payloads with toEqual.
Record:
- text = JSON.stringify(packet). packet is the complete response object built so far, i.e. exactly what is served minus servedContext.
- packetId = 'sha256:' + createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex'), from node:crypto.
- await recordContextReceipt(state, {...}). Pass approvedPlanRevision only when it is non-null.
- On success, serve JSON.parse(text) as the packet. It is a detached copy, so the bytes the adapter serializes are exactly the digested ones. Return receiptStatus 'recorded' with receiptId and packetId.
- On ANY error: logger.warn({ err, taskId, attemptId }, ...). Return the original packet with receiptStatus 'record-failed', receiptId null and packetId null.
DoD3 follows: no receipt id is ever served without a successful attempt write, and the context itself is still served in every profile.

(e) In the handler, build the existing response object unchanged into a const.
- A taskless read returns it as before.
- With a task, return `{ ...packet, servedContext }`, with servedContext appended last: { taskId, planRevision, approvedPlanRevision, attemptId, generation, receiptStatus, receiptId, packetId }.

(f) Extend the tool description: name servedContext and sessionId, and say that a receipt records what was served, never approval. Constraint: getContext.test.ts fails any tool description or inputSchema matching /full[- ](?:task )?context|full `?get_context/i. Write 'view:"full" read', never that phrase.

Tests: append to packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContextReceipt.test.ts.
Setup:
- beforeEach: vi.stubEnv('MOE_WORKER_ID', '') and vi.stubEnv('MOE_TASK_ID', ''). afterEach: vi.restoreAllMocks and vi.unstubAllEnvs.
- Seed worker-r and task-1, WORKING, assigned to worker-r, planRevision 3, approvedPlanRevision 3. Open the attempt via openAttempt for worker-r.
- Read durability from h.moePath/attempts/<id>.json.
Cases:
1. it.each over default and view 'full':
   - servedContext toStrictEqual { taskId 'task-1', planRevision 3, approvedPlanRevision 3, attemptId, generation 1, receiptStatus 'recorded', receiptId matching /^ctxreceipt-[0-9a-f]{32}$/, packetId matching /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/ }.
   - The file's contextReceipt toStrictEqual { id, packetId, taskId, attemptId, generation 1, workerId 'worker-r', sessionId, planRevision 3, approvedPlanRevision 3, view, servedAt: any String }.
   - It is unchanged after `await h.state.load()`.
   - packetId equals the sha256 of JSON.stringify(the response minus servedContext).
2. view 'status' with a valid sessionId on the same eligible attempt: no servedContext key, the attempt file bytes are identical, and writeEntity gets no 'attempts' call.
3. Rebinding:
   - A second read with another sessionId replaces the receipt: a new id, and the stored sessionId is the new one.
   - After planRevision advances to 4 (a definitionOfDone change through h.state.updateTask; seed directly if a guard refuses), the next receipt records planRevision 4 and keeps approvedPlanRevision 3 as history.
4. Ineligible cases, it.each. Each asserts receiptStatus, null receiptId and packetId, and no attempt write:
   - no sessionId → 'no-session'
   - no attempt → 'no-running-attempt'
   - attempt finalizing, reconciling or closed (setAttemptPhase) → 'no-running-attempt'
   - caller worker-x → 'not-attempt-owner'
   - task assigned to worker-y with worker-r's attempt → 'not-attempt-owner'
   - anonymous caller with a session → 'not-attempt-owner'
   - stored planRevision -1 → 'identity-unreadable', planRevision null, no throw
5. DoD3, it.each over attempt snapshots {version 2, profile 'legacy', planRevision 3, deliveryPolicy 'legacy'} and {version 2, profile 'verified-local', planRevision 3, deliveryPolicy 'local-branch'}:
   - writeEntity rejects only kind 'attempts'. Use the bind + mockImplementation pass-through from attemptStore.test.ts ~:58, because contextFetchedBy writes the task first.
   - get_context still resolves, with receiptStatus 'record-failed', receiptId null and packetId null.
   - The in-memory attempt has no contextReceipt, and the file bytes are unchanged.
   - readContextReceipt(currentAttempt(h.state, 'task-1')?.contextReceipt) is undefined.
6. Malformed sessionId, it.each over ['', '  ', 7, null, {}, 'a\nb', 'x'.repeat(256)] × views [undefined, 'status']: rejects /sessionId/, contextFetchedBy is unchanged and the attempt file is unchanged.

Delivery: getContext.ts is a CONTESTED path. Follow the Delivery note.

Verification: run the full daemon suite once, fresh. This task changes a shared schema and the MCP contract, so run the full suite, not just the new test file:
`cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test`
It must exit 0, and its command, exit code and output tail are complete_task's verification evidence.

Also run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit`, which must exit 0. Tests are excluded from tsconfig. Do NOT run `npm run build`: its prebuild regenerates the generated files.

Environment:
- On WSL, use a native Linux node_modules in a snapshot and never overwrite the shared Windows node_modules (mem gotcha-linux-vitest-reuse-native-node-modules).
- Unset the MOE_* seat env.
- For a failure outside this diff, re-run that file alone and on pristine HEAD before classifying it. waitForTask.test.ts:344 is a known load flake.

Size: measure `git diff --numstat -- packages/` plus `wc -l` of the new test file. The total must stay at or under 400 net changed lines, QA's oversize threshold; aim for about 350, with tests about 160 lines and table-driven.

Adversarial self-review of this task's diff only (adversarial-self-review skill). Fix whatever it finds. If anything changed, re-run step 4's command fresh before complete_task.

Check:
1. No path serves a receiptId or packetId without a successful attempt write. Inject a failure at writeEntity, and also inside recordContextReceipt's validation.
2. view:'status' and every non-recorded status write nothing under .moe/attempts.
3. A receipt binds only the STORED attempt's taskId, attemptId, generation and workerId, and only for a running attempt the caller owns while the task is assigned to that caller.
4. No process.env session read. A malformed sessionId is refused before contextFetchedBy is stamped, and null is refused rather than treated as absent.
5. get_context never throws on a hand-edited planRevision or attempt record.
6. The attempt byte pins still pass: claimNextTask.test.ts 'writes a claim that sends no identity byte for byte as before', and the finalizeAttempt.test.ts open-key-set pin. detached() returns the same object for a record with neither a receipt nor a snapshot.
7. No description or inputSchema text matches the FULL_READ regex.
8. Every edited contested path (schema.ts, getContext.ts) has a TOOL witness from this session (Delivery note).
9. complete_step.modifiedFiles lists all four files.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) A new receipt entity or store: rejected. The task and rails say to persist on existing attempts, with no second store or revision authority.
2) A receipt history list per attempt: rejected for one latest-wins `contextReceipt` slot. The record stays bounded, and the current receipt is what F07 step entry needs.
3) Binding the runner identity (processStartedAt/host, already on the attempt): rejected. It is constant across CLI respawns, and worker seats unset it. The receiving process/session incarnation is instead a caller-presented `sessionId`. The wrapper already mints MOE_SESSION_ID `<workerId>@<preflight-iso>` once per CLI launch (record_commit's sessionId, the Moe-Session trailer), so F09/F10 can transport it unchanged. There is no env fallback, because the daemon never derives a receiver identity.
4) A random packet id: rejected for a content digest, sha256 of the served payload minus servedContext, so a packet id names exactly what was served. That is what C01 extends and what deltas need.
5) Throwing from get_context when the receipt write fails under a strict profile: rejected. Serve the context with receiptStatus 'record-failed' and no ids. F07 refuses strict step entry without a current receipt.
6) Minting receipts without a session id: rejected. DoD2 requires the session binding. It also keeps every existing caller and the attempt byte pins unchanged, since nothing writes to an attempt until a session id is presented.
7) Updating docs/MCP_SERVER.md and SCHEMA.md here: deferred to F12, which owns the epic docs sweep; I01 and c2cb5cf7 also declare MCP_SERVER.md. The contract lives in the tool description/inputSchema, this plan and the handoff memory.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- attemptStore mutations go validate → writeEntity → map.set, so a failed write publishes nothing. recordAttemptPresence is the template; setAttemptPhase is not, because lastPhaseAt is the reconcile clock. Named refusals reuse numeric codes with an explicit codeName, so no enum edit is needed.
- get_context runs under the global mutex (McpAdapter runExclusive), and the adapter serializes the result with compact JSON.stringify.
- view:'status' returns early through util/contextStatus.ts, before any write.
- Existing tests never pass sessionId, so they cause no attempt writes. The attempt byte pins are claimNextTask.test.ts 'writes a claim that sends no identity byte for byte as before' and finalizeAttempt.test.ts ~:127.
- getContext.test.ts compares whole payloads ('preserves complete default context when full is explicitly selected' and the worker-vs-unknown-role case), so an unrecorded servedContext must be deterministic. Its FULL_READ test scans every tool description and inputSchema.
- decodeStoredPlanRevision (state/taskStore.ts:66) throws on a malformed stamp. approvedPlanRevision is a number or absent, stamped by F04/F05.
- validateStringValue (state/validators.ts) is the no-coercion string rule; validators.ts imports only leaf modules.
- Failure-injection idiom: attemptStore.test.ts ~:58. STRICT snapshot: ~:385.
- All four files are LF.

Make the edits to both files that way, or finish with a witnessed Edit round trip proven byte-identical (git hash-object before and after).

Other risks:

- Seat env leaks into vitest: stub MOE_WORKER_ID and MOE_TASK_ID.
- A writeEntity mock must pass 'tasks' writes through, because contextFetchedBy writes the task.
- Never run `npm run build`.

- F07 reads receipts via readContextReceipt and reads approval from the task, never from the receipt.
- F09 stamps sessionId and the attempt identity in the proxy.
- F10/F11 pass MOE_SESSION_ID on the preflight get_context and move postflight/adoption lookups to view:'status'.
